title: One Rule, and Where It Stops

scenes.tts: We have moved borders many ways. Can one idea tie the results together?
scenes.visual: Title card: One Rule, and Where It Stops. A grid of small tiles, each holding a mini map. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: We have moved borders many ways. Can one idea tie the results together?

scenes.tts: More F G F eight at the front: the barrel field moved back.
scenes.caption: More FGF8 at the front: the barrel field moved back.
scenes.visual: Tile: FGF8 up, arrow back.
scenes.narration: More FGF8 at the front: the barrel field moved back.

scenes.tts: F G F eight blocked: it moved forward.
scenes.caption: FGF8 blocked: it moved forward.
scenes.visual: Tile: FGF8 blocked, arrow forward.
scenes.narration: FGF8 blocked: it moved forward.

scenes.tts: A new source at the back: a partial second barrel field.
scenes.visual: Tile: second lamp, second patch of barrels.
scenes.narration: A new source at the back: a partial second barrel field.

scenes.tts: No E M X two: the front-and-middle areas grew back, and the visual area shrank.
scenes.caption: No Emx2: the front-and-middle areas grew back, and the visual area shrank.
scenes.visual: Tile: Emx2 lost, arrow back.
scenes.narration: No Emx2: the front-and-middle areas grew back, and the visual area shrank.

scenes.tts: More E M X two, same slope: the visual area grew, with total size unchanged.
scenes.caption: More Emx2, same slope: the visual area grew, with total size unchanged.
scenes.visual: Tile: Emx2 raised, arrow forward, outline unchanged.
scenes.narration: More Emx2, same slope: the visual area grew, with total size unchanged.

scenes.tts: No thalamic axons: marker borders in place at birth.
scenes.visual: Tile: Gbx2, no axons, borders unchanged.
scenes.narration: No thalamic axons: marker borders in place at birth.

scenes.tts: New input: barrels in grafted visual tissue, and an orientation map in auditory cortex.
scenes.visual: Tile: graft with barrels; tile: ferret auditory cortex with orientation patches.
scenes.narration: New input: barrels in grafted visual tissue, and an orientation map in auditory cortex.

scenes.tts: Which factor's loss and gain results did not mirror each other?
scenes.visual: A Pax6 tile appears face down. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Which factor's loss and gain results did not mirror each other?

scenes.tts: Pax six. Losing it shifted the markers, but raising it barely moved the map.
scenes.caption: Pax6. Losing it shifted the markers, but raising it barely moved the map.
scenes.visual: The Pax6 tile turns over: one arrow for loss, a flat line for gain.
scenes.narration: Pax6. Losing it shifted the markers, but raising it barely moved the map.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea that ties them together. Position draws the sketch; input finishes it.
scenes.visual: The rule appears on screen: position draws the sketch; input finishes it.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea that ties them together. Position draws the sketch; input finishes it.

scenes.tts: Each progenitor's position is recorded as levels of graded signals and transcription factors.
scenes.visual: The lamp and the Emx2 ramp beneath the map.
scenes.narration: Each progenitor's position is recorded as levels of graded signals and transcription factors.

scenes.tts: In our working model, a border falls where a level crosses a threshold. Change the dose, and the border slides.
scenes.visual: Threshold crossings slide as the lamp dims and brightens. A small corner label: working model.
scenes.narration: In our working model, a border falls where a level crosses a threshold. Change the dose, and the border slides.

scenes.tts: Add a second source, and part of the pattern can repeat.
scenes.visual: A second lamp at the back; a second crossing can appear.
scenes.narration: Add a second source, and part of the pattern can repeat.

scenes.tts: Thalamic input then sharpens the sketch, tells primary areas from higher-order ones, and helps shape the maps inside.
scenes.visual: Axons arrive; borders sharpen; primary and higher-order visual areas separate; inner maps tighten.
scenes.narration: Thalamic input then sharpens the sketch, tells primary areas from higher-order ones, and helps shape the maps inside.

scenes.tts: And the strongest evidence for a factor: loss and gain that move borders in opposite directions. A missing converse result does not rule a factor out.
scenes.visual: On screen: strongest evidence, loss and gain in opposite directions.
scenes.narration: And the strongest evidence for a factor: loss and gain that move borders in opposite directions. A missing converse result does not rule a factor out.

scenes.tts: The rule has limits. It covers where the primary area borders sit, front to back, in the mouse.
scenes.visual: A frame around the front-to-back axis of the mouse map. Label: what the rule covers.
scenes.narration: The rule has limits. It covers where the primary area borders sit, front to back, in the mouse.

scenes.tts: It does not cover total cortical growth, which some of these factors also change.
scenes.visual: A growing outline, crossed out of the frame.
scenes.narration: It does not cover total cortical growth, which some of these factors also change.

scenes.tts: Its threshold model does not explain the maps inside an area. Input and activity build those with the cortex's own cells.
scenes.visual: Barrels and orientation patches, set outside the frame, with arrows from both the thalamus and the cortex's own cells.
scenes.narration: Its threshold model does not explain the maps inside an area. Input and activity build those with the cortex's own cells.

scenes.tts: And it is drawn from mice. It does not claim to explain area sizes in primates or humans.
scenes.visual: A primate brain outline, outside the frame.
scenes.narration: And it is drawn from mice. It does not claim to explain area sizes in primates or humans.

scenes.tts: One question stays open. A gradient is smooth, yet mature borders are sharp.
scenes.visual: Last frame: a smooth ramp beside a sharp border, a question mark between them.
scenes.narration: One question stays open. A gradient is smooth, yet mature borders are sharp.

scenes.tts: How does the smooth gradient become a sharp border? And how much happens in progenitors, and how much in neurons under input?
scenes.visual: The question mark holds; progenitors on one side, neurons with thalamic axons on the other.
scenes.narration: How does the smooth gradient become a sharp border? And how much happens in progenitors, and how much in neurons under input?

scenes.tts: The takeaway: position draws the sketch, and input finishes it. How the sketch becomes a sharp line is not yet fully understood.
scenes.visual: The rule on screen above the smooth ramp and the sharp border.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: position draws the sketch, and input finishes it. How the sketch becomes a sharp line is not yet fully understood.
